methodologyNotes: Products independently re-verified against official manufacturer product pages (Philips Hue US, LIFX, Govee US, Wyze, TP-Link Tapo, Nanoleaf US shop, GE Lighting/Cync, WiZ Connected, Kasa Smart) and corroborating retailers/reviews (Best Buy, PCWorld, Matter Alpha, Amazon, Home Depot). All 13 drafted models are real and retained; none removed. Two spec corrections applied: (1) Hue White A19 75W is FIXED 2700K warm white, not tunable_white; (2) Nanoleaf Essentials A19 does NOT require a hub for basic use (works standalone over Bluetooth), so hub_required corrected to false to match the stated definition. hub_required is a boolean: true means a separate hub/bridge is mandatory for ANY use; false means the bulb pairs directly via its native app over Bluetooth or Wi-Fi. priceUsd reflects published US MSRP or list price for a single bulb; multi-pack unit prices are noted. accessedAt 2026-06-19.

products.name: TP-Link Tapo L535E Smart Wi-Fi Light Bulb (Matter)
products.priceNote: List price $17.99 for a single bulb at the official TP-Link Tapo US store (us.store.tapo.com); currently on sale there for $14.99. The tp-link.com manufacturer product page does not list a US price.
products.provenance: Confirmed the exact model on the official TP-Link US product page for the Tapo L535E V3 (1-pack), whose US technical specification table verbatim lists Form Factor "A19, E26", Brightness "1100 Lumens", Color Temperature Range "2500-6500 K" (multicolor + tunable white → rgbw), "Max. Power Consumption 9.5 W", "Lifetime 25,000 Hrs", Input Voltage "120 V~, 60 Hz", Wireless "IEEE 802.11b/g/n, 2.4 GHz WiFi Only; Bluetooth (only for setup)", "Compatible with Matter Yes", and "No Hub Required"; FCC/ETL/DOE/CEC certs confirm this is the US A19/E26 120V variant, distinct from the international A60/E27 220-240V/1055lm/8.6W version served on the bare URL. The official TP-Link Tapo US store independently corroborates the same L535E model at 1100 lumens and prices a single bulb at $17.99 (on sale $14.99). Price is sourced from the Tapo US store; wattage_w uses the stated 9.5 W max power consumption; no release date is published on either page so releaseDate/release are null.

products.name: SwitchBot Color Bulb
products.priceNote: US$15.99, single bulb (1-pack), listed on switch-bot.com (SwitchBot International store)
products.provenance: Fetched the official SwitchBot product page (switch-bot.com/products/switchbot-color-bulb) and its spec page (/pages/switchbot-color-bulb), which confirm this exact model "SwitchBot Color Bulb" (Shopify handle switchbot-color-bulb, listing created 2021-09-28): 1-pack US$15.99, "Energy-saving 10W bulb" with "up to 25,000 hours" lifespan, 16 million colors across 2700K-6500K tunable white, control via Wi-Fi 2.4GHz (IEEE 802.11 b/g/n) + Bluetooth (BLE 4.2), and "There's no need for a Hub" (hub_required=false). The digiblurDIY device wiki corroborates the exact US variant (model W1401400) as an "RGB+CT E26 800 lumen bulb", which is the source for base=e26 and brightness_lumens=800 since the manufacturer marketing pages state these only qualitatively. Price is SwitchBot's own listed US-dollar 1-pack figure; the international storefront currently surfaces the B22 style variant, but the $15.99 1-pack price and all electrical specs (10W, 25,000h, 2.4GHz Wi-Fi + BLE) are shared with the E26 US model.

products.provenance: Confirmed the exact model on the Aqara official product and specs pages (title "Aqara LED Bulb T1 (Tunable White)", Model Number LEDLBT1-L01): the /specs/ table states Luminous Flux 806lm, Rated Power 8.5W, Color Temperature 2700K-6500K (tunable white, Ra90 CRI), Bulb Interface E27, and Wireless Protocol "Zigbee, Bluetooth" (Zigbee 3.0 with repeater functionality; Matter support after release). Corroborated on PFE Technologies (Aqara's Singapore distributor), which lists the same model as a "Classic E27" tunable-white bulb with 806 lm output, Zigbee 3.0 + Bluetooth, and HomeKit Adaptive Lighting. hub_required=true because both pages describe the bulb connecting to the internet through Aqara Zigbee hubs with no standalone-control claim (consistent with the catalog's Sengled Zigbee entry); no US MSRP is published for this global E27 model so priceUsd is null (reseller prices were S$29.00 and RM99.00, non-USD), and neither lifespan hours nor a release year appears on any fetched page, so both are left null.

The Sengled manufacturer store URL for this exact model returns an HTTP 402 bot-protection code to automated fetchers, so specs were taken from the Amazon corroboration; no verbatim US-dollar price was observable (the Amazon page rendered a Germany-delivery price of EUR 14.88, and Best Buy was Sold Out), so priceUsd is null, and lifespan_hours and release year are not stated on any fetched page so both are null.

On price, the manufacturer lists this bulb only as a 2-pack at $48.99 with no single-bulb MSRP, so priceUsd is honestly null; Best Buy (SKU 5101600) and Home Depot (model 461004) single-bulb pages bot-blocked automated fetch (abort/403), so corroboration is null.
